title: W nowej pracy · miejscownik
title_en: Adjectives in the Locative · -ym, and -ej again
note:
B2 Block 2, unit 3 of 6 (spine O2). ONE new ending: -ym for masculine and neuter. The feminine -ej is the form b2_adj_gen taught one unit ago, unchanged.

FOUR NEW FORMS IN THE WHOLE UNIT: dobrym, nowym, małym, zimnym (all verified NEW with check_new.py). The same four adjectives as b2_adj_gen — dobry, nowy, mały, zimny — deliberately, so the block reads as one paradigm widening rather than a growing word list. dobrej, nowej, małej, zimnej all report TAUGHT <- b2_adj_gen [path 135] and are recycled, never re-taught.

THE UNIT'S CENTRAL CONTRAST, and the reason it can be this small: the Genitive and the Locative disagree about which word moves, and they disagree in opposite directions depending on gender.
- Feminine: the ADJECTIVE is the same in both cases and the NOUN is not — do dobrej szkoły vs w dobrej szkole.
- Masculine like dom: the NOUN is the same in both cases (domu is Genitive and Locative alike) and only the ADJECTIVE marks the difference — do nowego domu vs w nowym domu.
That minimal pair is slide 4 and it is what the Kontrola stage is built on. It is also why this unit sits immediately after b2_adj_gen and not anywhere else.

NO NEW GOVERNORS. All three Locative triggers are already owned and were checked as whole chunks, not assumed: w and na (a1_prep_place, a1_prep_review_1/2, a2_house) and o (a2_o_loc, which supplies o domu / o sklepie / o pracy / o banku wholesale). The only change is that the adjective now comes along.

A SPINE EXAMPLE HAD TO BE REJECTED. B2-SPINE's own illustration for this unit was 'Myślę o dobrym filmie.' — but check_new.py reports filmie as NEW (the course owns film, filmy, filmów and has never inflected it). wodzie, mleku, samochodzie and restauracji are NEW for the same reason, which rules out the other obvious Locative phrases. The unit runs on attested Locative noun forms only: domu, sklepie, biurze, hotelu, salonie, banku, mieście, mieszkaniu, biurku, pracy, szkole, firmie, kuchni.

FENCED:
- -emu appears nowhere, not in a slide and not as a distractor. b2_adj_dat owns it, two units away.
- No plural oblique adjectives (dobrych, dobrymi) — spine O3 sends those to C1.
- nowe and duże are used nowhere at all, including as distractors, despite both reporting TAUGHT: a2_plural_nom taught them as PLURALS, and the neuter singular slots take dobre and małe instead. This is b2_adj_acc's standing line and b2_work held it too.
- zimne and stare are NEW and appear nowhere.

DISTRACTORS are real taught Polish in the wrong slot, never fabricated. The oblique distractors are the Genitive forms taught last unit (nowego, małego, dobrego, zimnego) and the Accusatives from two units back (nową, małą, dobrą, zimną), which makes every wrong choice a genuine near-miss rather than noise. The two full-sentence items use wrong combinations of real forms so each explain can name which half failed to move.

QUIZ ANSWERS ARE ALL DISTINCT — eight single forms plus one Genitive-vs-Locative discrimination item and one full sentence.

intro.title: One new ending: -ym, for masculine and neuter
intro.body: You have been saying w domu, w sklepie, o pracy since your very first lessons — the noun's form for talking about where something is, or what you are talking about. What you have never had is the adjective in front of it. For masculine and neuter words it is one ending, -ym, and there are no exceptions among the words you own.

intro.title: The feminine form has not changed at all
intro.body: Last lesson you learned -ej for feminine words. That is also the form here — the same four words, doing a different job. So the feminine half of this lesson is nothing new to memorise. Notice what that means: the noun moves between the two cases and the adjective does not. do dobrej szkoły, but w dobrej szkole — szkoły became szkole, and dobrej just stayed where it was.

intro.title: Where it turns up — three words you already use
intro.body: There is nothing new to learn about when to use this form. Three little words you have had for a long time already pull the noun into it; from now on they pull the adjective too.
intro.body_pl: w nowym domu · na nowym biurku · o nowej pracy

intro.title: The one place to look twice
intro.title_pl: do nowego domu · w nowym domu
intro.body: These two cases can look almost identical, and which word gives the game away depends on the gender. With dom the noun is domu either way — so the adjective is the only thing telling you which one you meant. With a feminine word it is the other way round: the adjective is dobrej either way, and the noun tells you.

quiz.explain: w takes this lesson's form, and dom is masculine, so -ym. nowego is last lesson's form — right after do, wrong after w, and here the noun domu looks the same either way, so the adjective is doing all the work.
Neuter words take -ym, exactly like masculine ones. Only the feminine has its own ending here.
hotel is masculine. The past tense changes nothing about the case — w still pulls the same form.
salon is masculine, so -ym. zimną is the object form from two lessons ago — it belongs after mam, not after w.
praca is feminine, and the feminine form is the one you already learned last lesson. nowym would be right in front of a masculine or neuter word.
Feminine, so -ej — unchanged from last lesson. The noun is what moved: szkoła became szkole here, and it was szkoły after do.
firma is feminine. Same ending as in dobrej kawy from last lesson — one form, two jobs.
Feminine again, so -ej. Compare the same sentence about the salon, which is masculine and takes zimnym.
This one is not this lesson's form. do still takes -ego, the same as it always did. Only w, na and o take -ym.

quiz.prompt: I live in a small city. →
quiz.explain: Both words have to move together. małego mieście moves the adjective the wrong way, mały mieście leaves it as a subject, and małym miasto leaves the noun behind.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Mum works in a new office.
Type: My brother lives in a small city.
use_items.answer: Mój brat mieszka w małym mieście.
accepts: Mój brat mieszka w małym mieście.
Mój brat mieszka w małym mieście

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad is at the new job today.
use_items.answer: Tata jest dzisiaj w nowej pracy.
accepts: Tata jest dzisiaj w nowej pracy.
Tata jest dzisiaj w nowej pracy

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The key is on the new desk.
Type: My sister is talking about the new shop.
use_items.answer: Moja siostra mówi o nowym sklepie.
accepts: Moja siostra mówi o nowym sklepie.
Moja siostra mówi o nowym sklepie

use_items.prompt_en: Type: We're thinking about the small school.
Type: Mum is in the cold kitchen, and Dad is in the cold living room.
use_items.answer: Mama jest w zimnej kuchni, a tata jest w zimnym salonie.
accepts: Mama jest w zimnej kuchni, a tata jest w zimnym salonie.
Mama jest w zimnej kuchni, a tata jest w zimnym salonie
use_items.explain: Same adjective, two genders: kuchnia is feminine and takes -ej, salon is masculine and takes -ym.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad is going to the new shop, but he works at a good company.
use_items.answer: Tata idzie do nowego sklepu, ale pracuje w dobrej firmie.
accepts: Tata idzie do nowego sklepu, ale pracuje w dobrej firmie.
Tata idzie do nowego sklepu, ale pracuje w dobrej firmie
use_items.explain: Two halves, two cases: do keeps last lesson's -ego, w takes this lesson's form — and here the feminine dobrej happens to look the same in both.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: I don't have a new house, but I live in a good flat.
use_items.answer: Nie mam nowego domu, ale mieszkam w dobrym mieszkaniu.
accepts: Nie mam nowego domu, ale mieszkam w dobrym mieszkaniu.
Nie mam nowego domu, ale mieszkam w dobrym mieszkaniu
use_items.explain: domu and mieszkaniu are both nouns that do not change between these two cases — so the adjective is the only thing marking which one you mean.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My parents were in a good hotel.
